tierJustification: harness instrument correction and gate wiring; no money path and no product code in the diff, so MID is the need. No TOP claimed.
headline: A LARGE PART OF THE PER-CYCLE HEAP GROWTH I HAVE BEEN REPORTING WAS MY OWN CDP SESSION. Releasing the inspector's hold before each floor sample flattens the steady-state delta from +18.79 MB to -3.66 MB, and the product still holds exactly one panel realm.

whatChanged.cut: deep console release is now the DEFAULT before every floor sample in the heap-cycle harness
whatChanged.why: With the Runtime domain enabled the inspector holds page objects as '(Global handles) / DevTools console'. An Error created inside a panel realm closes over that realm through its stack accessor, so our own session pins dead realms. A harness that pins the object it measures cannot grade a fix to it.
whatChanged.shallowReleaseDoesNothing: Runtime.discardConsoleEntries + releaseObjectGroup('console') both returned ok on every cycle and freed nothing: 4 product-held vs 8 console-held realms, identical to the control.

killSwitch.effect: restores the old behaviour of releasing nothing
killSwitch.testableAgainstAbsent: absent env means enabled; verified absent=deep, '1'=false, '0'/'true'=deep
killSwitch.flippableWithoutReload: read per run, no build step

measurement.surface: deployed b99, distinct datasets (4/4 observed every cycle), PO workload armed playing=4 every cycle, 3 cycles

steadyStateDeltaSummary.honestLimit: n=2 with a 13 MB spread. The drop is about an order of magnitude and the direction is consistent, but I cannot put a tight number on the residual product rate from two cycles-pairs. Do not quote 2.81 as a rate.
steadyStateDeltaSummary.corroboration: snapshot sizes move the same way without going through usedJSHeapSize at all: control 308.3 -> 356.8 MB across the two graded cycles, deep release 289.1 -> 266.8 MB and 271.4 -> 269.9 MB.

measurement.constantAcrossAllRuns: product-retained is 1 in every run graded, always cycle1/panelB, always by the same _mcHostCacheFileRefOwners path. The product leak is unaffected by the instrument fix, which is why W79's answer stands.
measurement.reading: The warm-up delta survives (+22.06 from cycle 1 to 2) but the steady-state delta goes to zero and slightly negative once the inspector lets go. The snapshot shrank with it, 289.1 MB at cycle 2 to 266.8 MB at cycle 3 — the heap really got smaller.

correctionsToOurOwnRecord.W78: the 20.87 MB/cycle attributed to one retained panel realm per cycle is INSTRUMENT-INFLATED. The mechanism is real — a retained realm carries its whole ~21 MB script set — but the per-cycle RATE was substantially our inspector holding dead realms, not the product retaining a new one each cycle.
correctionsToOurOwnRecord.W76: the 23.28 +/- 2.73 MB/cycle that was said to close the calibration gap against the PO's ~13 carries the same inflation. It was measured with the inspector holding realms.
correctionsToOurOwnRecord.whatSurvivesUnchanged: W79's answer to which realm survives: panel B, constant across four runs, slot-bound not data-bound, product-anchored by host Chart._mcHostCacheFileRefOwners. The deep-release run still shows product-retained=1 naming cycle1/panelB by the same path, so the product leak is real and is NOT an artifact.
correctionsToOurOwnRecord.revisedShape: one panel realm pinned permanently by a host registry (bounded, ~21 MB), not one realm per cycle. The unbounded-growth claim does not survive this measurement.

openDiscrepancy.statement: The PO measures ~13 MB/cycle by hand with no automation, so his number cannot be inspector inflation. After removing our artifact our steady-state delta is ~0, so we now UNDER-read him where we used to over-read him.
candidates: the PO's session runs longer and touches more distinct datasets than a 3-cycle harness run
the PO reads process memory (Task Manager / Memory panel), which includes GPU, canvas and renderer overhead that usedJSHeapSize never sees
a product mechanism the harness workload does not reach
openDiscrepancy.notClaimed: I am not claiming the PO's leak is unreal. DECL-01: an instrument or the PO says so, and neither has said so.
openDiscrepancy.nextTest: same 3-cycle deep-release run with the PO's own reading method side by side, so both numbers come off one session.

gateWiring.cell: REALM-SURVIVAL-V1 now runs inside the heap-cycle memory gate whenever a run writes a snapshot
gateWiring.policy: a product-retained torn-down peer realm is a BLOCKING failure naming the panel and the retainer path; inspector-retained realms are reported and never graded; the kill switch reports SKIPPED non-blocking; a grade that cannot run FAILS rather than silently passing
gateWiring.childProcess: grading spawns node --max-old-space-size=10240 because a ~340 MB snapshot needs more old-space than the gate is launched with
gateWiring.gate01: RED on known-defective input: b99 today, naming cycle1/panelB and the full _mcHostCacheFileRefOwners path
gateWiring.forManagerA: grade a cut in one command: node --max-old-space-size=10240 scripts/realm-survival-gate.mjs --snapshot=<run>.cycle3.heapsnapshot --json — GREEN means no torn-down peer realm is product-reachable

defectFoundAndFixedInMyOwnWiring.what: the first in-line grade killed the run that produced it. The child took ~3.3 GB while the gate process was still holding parsed steady-state snapshots, and the gate died with no stdout after 4.5 minutes of browser work.
defectFoundAndFixedInMyOwnWiring.fix: child capped at 6144 MB, and the gate refuses to grade in-process when its own heapUsed is above 1.5 GB — emitting SKIPPED-LOWMEM with the exact standalone command instead. An unmeasurable heap counts as unaffordable rather than assumed safe.
defectFoundAndFixedInMyOwnWiring.rule: a grade is never worth losing the run that produced it; a skip that names its command is honest, a dead run is not.
defectFoundAndFixedInMyOwnWiring.tests: 4 unit tests on the guard and command, 36 passing in the memory/realm suites

escalation: BLOCKER: the product source for Chart._mcHostCacheFileRefOwners is not in this repo (searched every file, all extensions, including ignored paths — only my own test and heap snapshots match). Deployed b99 is ahead of the tree. Manager A or B unblocks by pointing me at the tree that builds b99, or A takes the cut with the path and gate I have handed over.
